name: The Miami escort William Wells brought from Fort Wayne
head: miami_escort_1812_01
review_note: review_required: a Miami man of the escort William Wells brought from Fort Wayne, whom no source names. The owner asked (2026-11-08) that each be given a researched, respectful name and a history, both marked reconstructed (liberty L-1812-native-cards-3507). Nothing of the fighting is staged in the scene.

present_on_scene_date.note: Each person's own card says how their presence on 14 August is known.

associated_with.note: The escort's camp ground on the prairie south-west of the fort, by the stables where their ponies (Currey: 'mounted on ponies') could be kept (T-3499); where they camped is not recorded. The rest of the 27 are carded at the same camp by T-3500.

not_in_this_household.note: Everyone the T-3463..T-3467 day readings put in this household is on the card (liberty L-1812-town-days-3463).

persons.name: Black Buzzard

age_band.note: An escort of fighting men: ages 22-41 spread across the eight; not recorded.

present_on_scene_date.note: Heald (1812): Wells arrived on the 13th with about 30 Miami. No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: In the town from 1812-08-13 to 1812-08-15: From Heald's date of arrival (13th) to the march out at 9 on the 15th, after which the escort left the field. Helm dates the arrival to the 12th and Wau-Bun and Currey to the 14th.

card_facts.label: On 15 August

history.title: A reconstructed history
history.caveat: No source tells this life: every particular of it is ours.
paragraphs: He came from the Miami towns about Fort Wayne on the upper Wabash and the Maumee, by Fort Wayne, and rode to Chicago with William Wells's escort, which reached the fort on the 13th.
He is of the Buzzard gens (Ah-pă′-kose-e-ă), and his children are of it after him.
He hunts deer in the oak openings, and in the fall goes after ducks and geese in the marshes of the Calumet.
At Chicago he camps with the escort south-west of the fort, with his pony.

card_evidence.locator: App. IV, Heald's report, Gutenberg #69274 lines 16229-16230
card_evidence.quote: On the 13th, Captain Wells, of Fort Wayne, arrived with about 30 Miamies, for the purpose of escorting us in
card_evidence.claim: Wells arrived on the 13th with about 30 Miami (Heald; the date this reading follows).

card_evidence.locator: App. VI, Helm's narrative, Gutenberg #69274 lines 16634-16635
card_evidence.quote: Capt. William Wells arrived from Fort Wayne on the 12th August with 27 Miamis
card_evidence.claim: Helm dates Wells to the 12th and counts 27 Miami.

card_evidence.quote: the arrival, on the 14th of August, of Captain Wells[33] with fifteen friendly Miamis.
card_evidence.claim: Wau-Bun's date for Wells: the 14th, with fifteen Miami.
card_evidence.tier: Kinzie family tradition (Wau-Bun; Quaife App. II judges its speeches and dialogue invented)

card_evidence.quote: a band of about thirty friendly Indians of the Miami tribe mounted on ponies
card_evidence.claim: Wells's Miami were mounted on ponies (Currey dates them to the 14th).

card_evidence.locator: App. IV, Heald's report, Gutenberg #69274 lines 16238-16240
card_evidence.quote: On the 15th, at 9 o'clock in the morning, we commenced our march: a part of the Miamies were detached in front
card_evidence.claim: The march began at 9 on the 15th, Miami in front and rear (Heald).

card_evidence.locator: pt. II, ch. II (VI, the right of bestowing names) and ch. VI (the gentes, notes 170 and 172)
card_evidence.quote: These names either proclaimed by their signification the gens to which they belonged, or were known as such by common reputation.
card_evidence.claim: how a reconstructed name is made
